name: Bylaw
description: A site-policy register like an open-source handbook: recommended cards, a filterable list grouped as Terms, Acceptable use, Privacy and Security, and documents with lettered clauses, a “what each section says” table, a breadcrumb and Copy as Markdown.
features: Preset: cards — grouped under Terms, Acceptable use, Privacy and Security, with a filter box always on
Lettered clauses (A., B., C.) written into the headings
A plain-language gloss under each clause, gathered into a summary table above the document
Breadcrumb trail (register / group / document) and an “In this article” rail
Print / PDF and Copy as Markdown on every document; edition history listed open
System font stack, light and dark
Zero custom CSS — every detail is a theme setting

metadata.seoDescription: The agreement that covers your use of Your Brand: accounts, content, fees and ending the agreement.

content.text: You own what you create. We run the Service for you, bill you for the plan you choose and give you 30 days to take your content with you if you leave.
Service — the Your Brand product and everything we host for you.
Content — anything you or your users upload or write in the Service.
Plan — the subscription you chose, with its limits and price.
Sample text for a fictional company, written to show the layout. It is not legal advice and not fit to publish as your own: replace every word with text your counsel has reviewed.
Who these terms are between
You, or the organization you sign up for, and Your Brand.
These terms are an agreement between Your Brand and the person or organization that creates an account (
you
). If you accept them for an organization, you confirm you are allowed to bind it.
Your account
Keep your login safe and tell us if somebody else gets in.
You are responsible for what happens under your account. Use a strong password, keep it to yourself and turn on two-step sign-in where we offer it.
Tell us at once if you think somebody has used your account without permission.
Using the Service
Use the product for lawful work and follow the acceptable use policy.
You may use the Service for your own business purposes, within your plan’s limits and in line with the
Acceptable Use Policy
. You may not:
resell or sublicense the Service unless we have agreed to it in writing;
try to get around usage limits, security controls or billing;
use the Service to build a product that copies it.
Your content
What you put in stays yours. We only use it to run the Service for you.
You keep every right you have in the content you put into the Service. You give us permission to host, copy and display it only as far as we need to run the Service for you.
We do not sell your content and we do not use it to train models for anyone else.
Fees and payment
Paid plans renew automatically until you cancel.
Paid plans are billed in advance and renew for the same period unless you cancel before the renewal date. Prices exclude taxes, which we add where the law requires.
If a payment fails we will tell you and try again. We may limit a paid feature if an invoice stays unpaid for 30 days after that notice.
Ending the agreement
Either side can end it; you get time to export your data.
You can close your account at any time from your settings. We may suspend or end your access if you seriously break these terms and do not fix it within 14 days of our notice.
After an account closes you have 30 days to export your content before we delete it.
Warranties and liability
The Service is provided as it is, and our liability is capped.

EXCEPT AS THESE TERMS SAY OTHERWISE, THE SERVICE IS PROVIDED “AS IS”. TO THE EXTENT THE LAW ALLOWS, EACH PARTY’S TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THESE TERMS IS LIMITED TO THE FEES YOU PAID IN THE 12 MONTHS BEFORE THE CLAIM.
Changes to these terms
We tell you before a change takes effect.
When we make a material change we publish the new edition with its effective date at least 30 days in advance and, where you have to accept it again, ask you on your next visit.
Governing law
Which law applies, and where disputes go.
These terms are governed by the law of Placeholder Jurisdiction. Its courts have exclusive jurisdiction over any dispute about them.
Questions about these terms: legal@example.com. We answer within five working days.

Nothing illegal, abusive or that exploits anyone.

Security and abuse
No attacks, scraping at scale or getting around limits.
Do not probe, scan or test the Service’s security without our written permission.
Do not send spam or use the Service to distribute malware.

What we collect
Account details, what you put in, and basic usage logs.
Account details
— your name, email address and billing details.
Content
— what you write or upload in the Service.
Usage data
— pages visited, features used, device and browser type, kept to run and improve the Service.
How we use it
To run the Service, support you and keep it secure — not to sell.
We use personal data to provide the Service, answer support requests, keep accounts secure and send the messages you ask for. We never sell personal data.
Who we share it with
Only vetted providers who help us run the Service.

Your rights

metadata.seoDescription: How we process personal data on your behalf: roles, security, sub-processors and breach notice.

content.text: When your content includes personal data, we only process it to run the Service for you, keep it secure and tell you quickly if something goes wrong.
Controller — the party that decides why and how personal data is processed.
Processor — the party that processes personal data on the controller’s behalf.
Breach — a security incident that leads to the loss of, or unauthorized access to, personal data.
Sample text for a fictional company, written to show the layout. It is not legal advice and not fit to publish as your own: replace every word with text your counsel has reviewed.
Roles
You decide what data goes in; we process it for you.
For personal data in your content, you are the controller and Your Brand is the processor. We process it only on your documented instructions, which are these terms and your use of the Service.
Security
We protect the data with technical and organizational measures.
We keep the data encrypted in transit and at rest, limit staff access to what a task needs, and test our controls every year.
Sub-processors
We tell you before we add a new one.
You authorize the sub-processors in our
list
. We give you 30 days’ notice of a new one, and you may object on reasonable grounds.
Breaches
We tell you without undue delay.
We notify you without undue delay, and within 72 hours, after becoming aware of a breach affecting your data, with what we know and what we are doing about it.
Deletion
When the agreement ends, the data is deleted.
When the agreement ends we delete the personal data within 90 days, unless the law requires us to keep it.
Ask for a countersigned copy at legal@example.com.

content.text: Found a security problem? Tell us privately, test only your own accounts, and we will keep you told.

Reporting a vulnerability
Write to us privately first.
If you believe you have found a security issue, write to security@example.com with the steps to reproduce it. Please do not publish it until we have fixed it.
Safe harbour
Good-faith research within these rules is welcome.
Test only against accounts you own.
Do not access, change or delete other people’s data.
Stop and tell us as soon as you find something.
What we promise
